evidence.excerpt: Three accelerated ageing protocols for thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) catheter tubing segments are compared: elevated temperature immersion (70 °C in phosphate-buffered saline), combined UV/humidity exposure (UVA, 0.76 W/m², 50% RH), and real-time ageing at 23 °C/50% RH over 52 weeks. Fatigue life under cyclic bending (displacement-controlled, 1 Hz, 180° bend radius) was measured for each protocol at nominal ageing equivalents of 6, 12, 24, and 52 weeks. The elevated temperature protocol was the most aggressive: fatigue life after 24-week equivalent ageing dropped to 42% of the initial value. Molecular weight (GPC), hardness (Shore A), and elongation at break were measured alongside fatigue data. Arrhenius correlation between the 70 °C and 23 °C datasets yielded an activation energy of 84 kJ/mol, within the range expected for hydrolytic degradation of polyester-based TPU. The UV/humidity protocol produced divergent results not predictable from the thermal model, suggesting a different degradation mechanism relevant only to external device surfaces.
